_about: Heat exchanger kit PREPARATION (parked kit #1481, milestone 58), all DRAFT. Box list and draft rule cards for a shell-and-tube heat exchanger datasheet, built only from the standards the library already holds: SAES-E-004 (shell and tube exchangers). Every card is a draft: no engineer has signed it off, no real exchanger document has proved it. Read only when `exchanger_kit_draft_enabled` is on (off by default); every result is held for the engineer. Rule text is in our own words, never the standard's. Clause numbers and pages are as stored in the library and not verified. A card whose value no held clause requires stays draft 'needs ...' (order 301.1, A-1440). TEMA, API 660 and API 661 (the standards the committed checklist names) are NOT held, so no card cites them. The other held exchanger standards (SAES-E-006 double pipe and hairpin, SAES-E-007 air-cooled, SAES-E-014 plate and frame, SAES-E-015) are for other exchanger types and are not used here. ASME VIII-1 is held, but 0 of its 4,073 stored rules carry ASME's own clause numbers, so no card cites an ASME clause.
standards_held_unusable_for_citation: ASME BPVC VIII-1 (clause numbers in the library are not ASME's own)

cards.text: The design code, with its division and edition, is stated on the data sheet.
The minimum design metal temperature is stated on the data sheet.
The tube wall thickness is stated on the data sheet.
The design pressure is stated on the data sheet.
The operating pressure is stated on the data sheet (the clause asks for both the normal and the maximum one).
The minimum corrosion allowance of the pressure components is stated on the data sheet.
The shell material is stated on the data sheet (the materials of construction).
The tube material is stated on the data sheet (the materials of construction).

The weld joint efficiency is at least 0.85 (85%). A figure printed as a percentage (70 or 85 %) is not judged: it is an engineer's question. Not checked: whether the exchanger is built to the Division 1 code this clause is written for.

tests.name: printed as a percentage at the limit

cards.text: The design pressure is at least 1.05 times the maximum operating pressure. Not checked: the larger factor of 1.1 (or the fixed offset of 15 psi) that the clause gives for a maximum operating pressure up to 6,900 kPa; the stored table text is garbled, so only the lowest factor in it is used. The check reads whichever operating pressure the sheet states, which may be the normal and not the maximum one. It reads one design pressure: the shell side and the tube side are each the clause's, so a sheet that prints two is an engineer's question.

tests.name: a different unit above the limit
a different unit below the limit

cards.text: The design temperature is at least 28 C above the operating temperature (the clause says the maximum operating temperature on the PFD). The margin is a fixed 28 C, with no percentage part. Not checked: whether the sheet's operating temperature is the maximum one rather than the normal one. A sheet printed in Fahrenheit is not judged: it is an engineer's question.
The test pressure is stated on the data sheet.
cards.needs: a clause that requires the test pressure to be stated (the cited clause only designs the supports for it; no SAES-E-004 clause asks for the value on the data sheet)

cards.text: The fouling resistance is stated on the data sheet.
cards.needs: a clause that requires the fouling resistance to be stated (the cited clause says where the value is chosen from, not that it is stated; the clause that gives a fixed value is only for two-pass shells and sea or well water)

cards.text: The TEMA type is stated on the data sheet.
cards.needs: a clause that requires the type to be stated (the cited clause says the TEMA nomenclature is used when specifying exchangers, not that the type letters are printed on the data sheet); TEMA itself is not held

cards.text: The allowable pressure drop is stated on the data sheet.
cards.needs: a clause that requires the ALLOWABLE pressure drop to be stated (the cited clause asks for the calculated pressure drop, clean and fouled, which is a different value)

cards.text: The tube length is stated on the data sheet.
cards.needs: a clause that requires the tube length to be stated (the cited clause only prefers standard lengths; it does not ask for the value)

cards.text: The heat duty is stated on the data sheet.
cards.needs: a clause that names the heat duty (the cited clause says the data sheet holds all the information the manufacturer needs, without naming the duty)
